correction: An earlier version of this table printed the index multiplied by 0.972757, the factor relating the two household coefficient sets. That was an error: the index is a ratio of two shares and is therefore invariant to any uniform rescaling of the coefficients, so the factor does not belong in it. The own-survey column was left unscaled, so the two columns were not even on one basis. Both are now the plain ratio of shares, which is exactly what the caption defines and what the printed share columns reproduce. Converting the index to claims per wage dollar requires the aggregate multiplier reported here, and the level is given in its own column.
